answer: An agent economy can price every identity action with a computational toll. Before an agent votes, attests, or claims rewards, it must solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle tied to the current epoch, like cracking a walnut whose shell regrows each round. The network accepts only answers that took measurable time, so fakes cannot ride one machine's effort; every puppet pays compute again. Honest agents keep a haven of headroom, while an attacker running sock puppets sees power bills scale linearly. The vault of rewards goes to provably spent work, not headcount, so sybils just buy losses.
